additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by one or more persistent, non-bizarre or somewhat plausible delusions lasting at least one month, in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked functional decline typical of schizophrenia. Outside the delusional themes, individuals often appear relatively intact, with preserved cognition, affect, and daily functioning, which can delay detection and treatment. Onset is typically in mid-to-late adulthood and may follow psychosocial stressors, interpersonal conflicts, or situations that can be misinterpreted and woven into a fixed false belief. It is distinguished from mood and psychotic disorders by the circumscribed nature of the beliefs, minimal other psychotic features, and relatively stable overall functioning.

patient.personality: Valerie is a methodical, intellectually curious, and somewhat solitary person who channels her energy into precision work, self-improvement, and quiet hobbies like reading, gardening, and meditation.
patient.stressor: About a year and a half ago, Valerie’s younger sister moved back to their hometown and into a closer relationship with their aging parents, leading to renewed family tensions that Valerie had largely avoided by living independently and focusing on her career. Long-standing feelings of being overlooked in the family resurfaced as her parents began asking her sister, rather than her, for help with decisions, while at work she was passed over for a supervisory training opportunity she had been informally preparing for. She started ruminating extensively about these slights and spending evenings replaying conversations, gradually coming to see routine family disagreements and ambiguous comments from coworkers as confirming a specific, fixed interpretation of how others were treating her that she could not let go of despite their explanations and alternative perspectives. Over the following year, this rigid view began to color her interactions, straining family gatherings and workplace relationships, and after a trusted coworker from her yoga group gently pointed out how stuck she seemed on these beliefs and suggested that it might help to talk to a professional, Valerie agreed to seek psychiatric consultation.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’ve gotten locked into certain beliefs about how people are treating me, and I can’t shake them even when they try to explain otherwise.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For the past year, no matter how many times my parents or coworkers tell me I’m overthinking it, I’m convinced my sister and a few people at work are quietly coordinating to edge me out—like when my supervisor “accidentally” leaves me off emails or my mom mentions a decision they already made with my sister, it just confirms to me that there’s this ongoing plan to keep me in the dark and make me look less competent.
